docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:89:Attempt transitions: `RESERVED → CALLING → VALIDATED | REJECTED | UNKNOWN_CALL`, followed by settled accounting and then `APPLIED | SUPERSEDED`. Reserve through actual `sessions.reserveModel` in the same short transaction that creates the attempt; dispatch provider I/O only after commit. A unique attempt prevents two coordinator threads from sending the same reservation twice. A bounded translator lease/claim serializes coordinator work and is subordinate to the existing worker fence and session deadline; it is not a second browser-ownership fence. Only the claimant can transition its committed attempt into the one provider-send authority. Losing that lease makes the result ineligible for acceptance even if the worker lease remains live. `reserveModel` is accounting only, and existing `internal()` may return a cached duplicate before active/source checks: never use a repeated reservation response as permission to send. The durable attempt claim separately rechecks current authorization, source, state, owner and deadline immediately before provider send and after response. Process restart with a persisted CALLING attempt treats its usage as unknown and retains the reservation ceiling; it never repeats that provider invocation under the same attempt. Any fresh read-only retry is a new fully charged attempt within the remaining shared budget.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:91:Reserve the bounded complete encoded request conservatively (UTF-8 bytes as an upper input-token reservation, including static schema/instruction overhead) and configured max output tokens. Reject oversized requests before reservation/transport; do not truncate essential source to fit. Each request and repair counts against the same `maxModelProposals`, total input/output, absolute session deadline and configured provider timeout. `settleModel` charges overage and never refunds a ceiling; missing usage settles unknown, retaining the reserved cost. Settlement keys are durable/idempotent. In a fresh transaction, lock session/source/translation in the stated order, settle known usage and accept/reject the result atomically against current source, worker fence, translator lease, observation and plan-head identity. An overage that fails the session prevents application of the result. Result validation outside the transaction never constitutes acceptance.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:93:**Late accounting without revival:** existing `settleModel` is active/owner guarded and cannot settle after cancellation/expiry. Do not weaken those guards. Retain the already charged reservation ceiling, mark the attempt abandoned/superseded, and append an immutable, attempt-scoped late-usage receipt through the translation store under its own accounting-only authorization. That operation can record numeric usage and whether known input/output exceeds the original reservation; it cannot change session state, plan head, owner, source, ledger or admission. Billing/evaluation reporting joins each reservation with its one accepted usage receipt and reports `max(reserved, known actual)` once per token category, so known overage is visible rather than described as capped or zero. Unknown actual usage remains explicitly unknown. If the session is still active but authority changed, continuation stays blocked until the current authorized coordinator reconciles accounting through the existing service; if that cannot safely occur, stop the run. A terminal session stays terminal. This is audit/reconciliation, not a second session budget counter or fresh send permit.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/translation-design.md:120:Before `prepareAndAdmit`, validate that the referenced obligation remains permitted/unfulfilled and that the proposed operation, current target correspondence and exact input/binding/argument meaning match its accepted definition. Reserve its coordinate, canonical proposal digest and deterministic admission idempotency key in the translation store under the session/source/translation lock order, then release locks before runner preparation. Bind the actual admission to that obligation atomically inside the existing admission transaction through the coordinated `GuidedSessionService` integration; use server-private persisted state keyed by the admission idempotency key. No OBS-004 action/runner wire field changes are needed. Changed operation/reference meaning cannot reuse the reserved association. Database uniqueness and single-assignment guards prevent concurrent callers from allocating another admission for the same obligation. A failed pre-admission preparation may retry only through the same reserved obligation/coordinate with no existing admission; it cannot erase a dispatched or successful association.

Replay jobs and `Execute3` carry run-scoped `secrets` and `secretOrigins`; `Launch3` carries the safe scope. `Execute3.inputs` pairs ordinary materialized entries with value-less `{inputId,stepId,kind:secretRef,intendedSlot:fill.value,referenceName}` metadata so the child resolves the declared secret ID and checks its declaring step without inferring an ID from inputId. Empty maps are valid. `Result3.secretUse` records only ID-keyed `USED`, `NOT_USED` or `REFUSED` codes. The reference grammar is `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$` throughout those maps.

docs/stories/10.6.story.md:64:- [x] **AC-10:** Capacity saturation (initial `POOL_SIZE=1`, §5.2) returns `429` with `Retry-After` and is a **definite non-acceptance**: no slot held, no admission request issued, no scratch created, no browser started, nothing durable anywhere. docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/t2-before-amendment-secret-login-design.md:109:**4.2 Password-only fill (SEC-6) — ruling, restated after security review F-1.** The collector never exports a password control (§1), so the model cannot name one and the earlier "`controlType:'password'` at observation" rule was unimplementable. Rule: the model emits `fill(secretRef)` with the node-free target `{kind:"passwordControl", documentId, generation}`; **trusted runner code** resolves the target at `prepare` and again at the moment of the fill — exactly one visible, enabled `input[type=password]` in the current top-level document (frames excluded), pinned as an element handle, origin-checked (§4.3), filled through that handle so a type-flip after resolution fails on the handle. 0 or >1 candidates ⇒ `POLICY_DENIED` with reason `PASSWORD_TARGET_ABSENT` / `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`; nothing typed. **Identity continuity (R1-1):** `generation` advances only per observation and `navigation` only on `framenavigated`, so a same-document DOM swap would otherwise let "re-resolve at fill" pick a different element. Resolution therefore runs **inside the collector's isolated world** under the existing `acquire`-style guard — cited `documentId`, `generation`, `observedNavigation === navigation` before and after the in-world call (`browser.ts:304-320`; `invoke` guard `:374`). The element pinned at `prepare` is retained in that world; the fill requires that **the same element** is still attached, still `type=password`, still the unique visible candidate, and that `location.origin` read **in that world** (not `page.url()`) is in `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins`; any deviation ⇒ `TARGET_CHANGED`, nothing typed; `navigation` is re-checked after the fill. **One function (R1-3):** "visible, enabled password input" is defined once in the isolated-world collector — computed-style visibility plus non-zero box (not viewport), traversal including open shadow roots (`observationCollector.ts:134-137,259-260,418-431`) — and that same function produces `coverage.passwordControls`, the `prepare` resolution and the fill-time check; a `querySelectorAll` resolver is forbidden. docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:99:### 4.1 Window reservation and settlement
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:101:1. On unavailable target and no open window, under current session/source lock reserve the **remaining** allowance: `reservedMs=min(allowanceMs-usedMs, floorMillis(sessionExpiry-now), floorMillis(currentOwnerLeaseExpiry-now))`. Require positive. Increment usedMs by reservedMs and persist one window with original openedAt, deadline=openedAt+reservedMs, lastCheckedAt=openedAt, uncertain=false. This is a reservation ceiling, not measured browser time. No model or human work runs while this window is open.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:104:4. Normal acknowledged refresh settlement validates the exact request/result and current authority. Clear pending once and commit NEXT; retain window and update lastCheckedAt and last observation identity. If still unavailable, the same window continues with its original deadline. If uniquely available or ordinary ambiguity now requires the existing clarification path, close the window **before** any model reservation: for a fully known window charge `min(reservedMs, max(0, ceilMillis(settledAt-openedAt)))`, release only its unused reserved portion once, and clear window. Used time remains cumulative. Clarification/model time after this commit is governed only by existing budgets.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:105:5. A recovered **unsettled pending request** marks window.uncertain=true before recovering its exact refresh; this flag is sticky. Its entire reservedMs remains charged on closure even if later evidence arrives. No refund of unknown work, no negative adjustment, no duplicate settlement. Normal scanner restart between settled polls (pending=null) resumes the same original open window/deadline and includes its downtime; it does not invent uncertainty or a new reservation. Concurrent scanners may conservatively retain a window's full reservation if one sees another's unsettled pending request. Safety does not depend on identifying a process crash perfectly.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:106:6. Deadline/count/byte exhaustion, cancellation, source/fence loss or unresolved completion retains all pending reservations and commits the stop decision/accounting. A late callback cannot reopen/extend a window or release a retained unknown charge. A known closed window cannot be settled again: compare windowId and pending poll identity atomically. An already-ready later obligation may proceed with zero remaining readiness allowance because it needs no passive wait; another unavailable target may not open a window. This prevents a hidden model/human timeout while still bounding every readiness episode.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:131:- Guided PostgreSQL scanner restart before/after pending refresh/callback, concurrent scanner requests and same-owner renewal preserve window deadline/count/key and used/reserved duration. Recover a callback committed before settlement using the exact original request despite advanced generation. Source/fence/plan/obligation edits refuse stale completion; no old model result is restamped. Clarification suspends polling, and its existing answer mapping stays exact.
docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/delayed-state-design.md:132:- With browser timeout1 second, an immediately ready target and valid model response delayed beyond1 second still succeed within existing call/session budgets. A human answer after browser timeout but within question/session expiry preserves its exact meaning; model/human time outside readiness windows is not charged. Two known readiness windows in one compound source step succeed when their cumulative charge fits; exhausted or unknown reservations cannot be reset/refunded by another operation, question, replan or reconnect.

Its `owner()` is `identity(OWNER, "60404", "owner")` and its drafts are created on `CSI_ID = "60404"`, so the new checks pass. By reading, it stays green. It is run in T-10.30.3 to show that. docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/bootstrap-closure-application/before/docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/secret-login-design.md:110:**4.2 Password-only fill (SEC-6) — ruling, restated after security review F-1.** The collector never exports a password control (§1), so the model cannot name one and the earlier "`controlType:'password'` at observation" rule was unimplementable. Rule: the model emits `fill(secretRef)` with the node-free target `{kind:"passwordControl", documentId, generation}`; **trusted runner code** resolves the target at `prepare` and again at the moment of the fill — exactly one visible, enabled `input[type=password]` in the current top-level document (frames excluded), pinned as an element handle, origin-checked (§4.3), filled through that handle so a type-flip after resolution fails on the handle. 0 or >1 candidates ⇒ `POLICY_DENIED` with reason `PASSWORD_TARGET_ABSENT` / `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`; nothing typed. **Identity continuity (R1-1):** `generation` advances only per observation and `navigation` only on `framenavigated`, so a same-document DOM swap would otherwise let "re-resolve at fill" pick a different element. Resolution therefore runs **inside the collector's isolated world** under the existing `acquire`-style guard — cited `documentId`, `generation`, `observedNavigation === navigation` before and after the in-world call (`browser.ts:304-320`; `invoke` guard `:374`). The element pinned at `prepare` is retained in that world; the fill requires that **the same element** is still attached, still `type=password`, still the unique visible candidate, and that `location.origin` read **in that world** (not `page.url()`) is in `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins`; any deviation ⇒ `TARGET_CHANGED`, nothing typed; `navigation` is re-checked after the fill. **One function (R1-3):** "visible, enabled password input" is defined once in the isolated-world collector — computed-style visibility plus non-zero box (not viewport), traversal including open shadow roots (`observationCollector.ts:134-137,259-260,418-431`) — and that same function produces `coverage.passwordControls`, the `prepare` resolution and the fill-time check; a `querySelectorAll` resolver is forbidden. Consequences stated: an off-screen but rendered decoy counts ⇒ ambiguous ⇒ refuse; frames and closed shadow roots are excluded ⇒ absent ⇒ refuse. **Form action (R1-2):** the fill is refused with `PASSWORD_FORM_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` when the pinned input's owning `form.action` (resolved URL) has an origin outside `allowedOrigins`, or when the input has no owning form and the document origin differs from the observed login document's origin. `GuidedProposalValidator` accepts `passwordControl` only with a `secretRef` value, only for an input whose `sourceStepId` is the fill's step, and only when the cited observation reports `coverage.passwordControls === 1`; the proposal's `executionEvidence` still binds document/generation, so staleness checks are unchanged (I-A1 holds). **Limit (stated; accepted at GA — user default 2026-10-09, ADR-SC-005):** pages with two or more visible password fields (change-password, registration with confirm) are not supported for `secretRef` fills — the author gets `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`, nothing is typed, and there is no fallback adapter; a model-supplied ordinal/form narrowing is a reserved extension requiring its own Security review. Likewise a secret into a non-password control (TOTP, API token into a text field) is unsupported: the rule has **no opt-out** on the single path (§8 Q1, decided). Accepted because Vault is `none` in every value set today (GA plan C-3) and no shared environment has ever been deployed (panel 2026-10-09, devops), so no production secret-filling test exists.

docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/architecture-application/before/docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/secret-login-design.md:110:**4.2 Password-only fill (SEC-6) — ruling, restated after security review F-1.** The collector never exports a password control (§1), so the model cannot name one and the earlier "`controlType:'password'` at observation" rule was unimplementable. Rule: the model emits `fill(secretRef)` with the node-free target `{kind:"passwordControl", documentId, generation}`; **trusted runner code** resolves the target at `prepare` and again at the moment of the fill — exactly one visible, enabled `input[type=password]` in the current top-level document (frames excluded), pinned as an element handle, origin-checked (§4.3), filled through that handle so a type-flip after resolution fails on the handle. 0 or >1 candidates ⇒ `POLICY_DENIED` with reason `PASSWORD_TARGET_ABSENT` / `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`; nothing typed. **Identity continuity (R1-1):** `generation` advances only per observation and `navigation` only on `framenavigated`, so a same-document DOM swap would otherwise let "re-resolve at fill" pick a different element. Resolution therefore runs **inside the collector's isolated world** under the existing `acquire`-style guard — cited `documentId`, `generation`, `observedNavigation === navigation` before and after the in-world call (`browser.ts:304-320`; `invoke` guard `:374`). The element pinned at `prepare` is retained in that world; the fill requires that **the same element** is still attached, still `type=password`, still the unique visible candidate, and that `location.origin` read **in that world** (not `page.url()`) is in `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins`; any deviation ⇒ `TARGET_CHANGED`, nothing typed; `navigation` is re-checked after the fill. **One function (R1-3):** "visible, enabled password input" is defined once in the isolated-world collector — computed-style visibility plus non-zero box (not viewport), traversal including open shadow roots (`observationCollector.ts:134-137,259-260,418-431`) — and that same function produces `coverage.passwordControls`, the `prepare` resolution and the fill-time check; a `querySelectorAll` resolver is forbidden. Consequences stated: an off-screen but rendered decoy counts ⇒ ambiguous ⇒ refuse; frames and closed shadow roots are excluded ⇒ absent ⇒ refuse. **Form action (R1-2):** the fill is refused with `PASSWORD_FORM_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` when the pinned input's owning `form.action` (resolved URL) has an origin outside `allowedOrigins`, or when the input has no owning form and the document origin differs from the observed login document's origin. `GuidedProposalValidator` accepts `passwordControl` only with a `secretRef` value, only for an input whose `sourceStepId` is the fill's step, and only when the cited observation reports `coverage.passwordControls === 1`; the proposal's `executionEvidence` still binds document/generation, so staleness checks are unchanged (I-A1 holds). **Limit (stated; accepted at GA — user default 2026-10-09, ADR-SC-005):** pages with two or more visible password fields (change-password, registration with confirm) are not supported for `secretRef` fills — the author gets `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`, nothing is typed, and there is no fallback adapter; a model-supplied ordinal/form narrowing is a reserved extension requiring its own Security review. Likewise a secret into a non-password control (TOTP, API token into a text field) is unsupported: the rule has **no opt-out** on the single path (§8 Q1, decided). Accepted because Vault is `none` in every value set today (GA plan C-3) and no shared environment has ever been deployed (panel 2026-10-09, devops), so no production secret-filling test exists.

docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/c-approved-tuple-guard-order/sources/docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/contracts/v3/README.md:7:`BridgeDispatch.secret` is a closed transient object present exactly for a secret fill: ID, value (1–4096), Vault version (1–256), and 1–16 origins (each at most 512). It is excluded from digest calculation. Idempotency separately binds the safe secret ID and source input ID; it never stores a value. Replay jobs and `Execute3` carry run-scoped `secrets` and `secretOrigins`; `Launch3` carries the safe scope. `Execute3.inputs` pairs ordinary materialized entries with value-less `{inputId,stepId,kind:secretRef,intendedSlot:fill.value,referenceName}` metadata so the child resolves the declared secret ID and checks its declaring step without inferring an ID from inputId. Empty maps are valid. `Result3.secretUse` records only ID-keyed `USED`, `NOT_USED` or `REFUSED` codes. The reference grammar is `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$` throughout those maps.
